records.image_0: RGB 256x256 PNG: the forward camera, one frame per 0.2 s step

action.name: forward_speed_m_s
action.definition: forward speed in the body frame, m/s

action.name: yaw_rate_rad_s
action.definition: yaw rate, rad/s, positive turning right (clockwise seen from above)

state.name: distance_to_target_m
state.definition: horizontal distance from the drone to the target's centre, m
state.privileged_reason: computed from the target's true position, which the drone cannot observe: a policy that reads it can fly to the target without the image or the instruction

state.name: bearing_to_target_rad
state.definition: bearing of the target relative to the drone's heading, rad in [-pi, pi], positive to the right (|r| 0.92 / 0.88 with a motion-based estimate on the real episodes)
state.privileged_reason: computed from the target's true position, which the drone cannot observe: a policy that reads it can fly to the target without the image or the instruction

state.name: altitude_minus_1_47_m
state.definition: altitude above ground minus 1.47 m (|r| 0.986 / 0.996; fitted 0.985 z - 1.470, 0.987 z - 1.477)

state.name: speed_m_s
state.definition: speed: the norm of the velocity vector, m/s

state.name: yaw_rate_rad_s
state.definition: yaw rate, rad/s, positive clockwise seen from above (|r| 0.54 / 0.76)

state.name: x_from_start_m
state.definition: x (north) relative to the episode's start, m

state.name: y_from_start_m
state.definition: y (east) relative to the episode's start, m

records.language_instruction: the episode's instruction, repeated on every step

step_definitions.action: float32[3]: forward m/s, yaw rate rad/s, vertical m/s (up)

episode_metadata.name: file_path
episode_metadata.meaning: <store>/episodes/<episode id>, as the release has it

episode_metadata.name: episode_id
episode_metadata.meaning: the episode's id in its store: <scene>_<seed>

episode_metadata.name: store
episode_metadata.meaning: the raw store (one scene and collection batch) it came from

episode_metadata.name: split_of_scene
episode_metadata.meaning: the scene's own split (train, test_seen, test_unseen); not the dataset split

episode_metadata.name: target_category
episode_metadata.meaning: vehicle, geometry, furniture, equipment, human or other (the paper's Fig. 3c mix)

episode_metadata.name: target_seen
episode_metadata.meaning: whether the target is in the seen pool (unseen targets are for test_unseen scenes)

episode_metadata.name: target_status
episode_metadata.meaning: the pool entry's status: primitive (engine shape), imported (a real model) or placeholder

episode_metadata.name: target_stand_in
episode_metadata.meaning: a low-poly stand-in (Kenney) for the object its name describes; filter on it to drop them

episode_metadata.name: seed
episode_metadata.meaning: the episode seed (start, target, distractors and layout follow from it and the scene)

episode_metadata.name: pilot
episode_metadata.meaning: sha256 of the expert checkpoint that flew it

split.rule: val takes round(val_fraction x episodes), at least one, given out one at a time to the scene x target stratum furthest below its share (val_fraction x its episodes; ties by sha256 of seed and stratum), never a stratum's last train episode; within a stratum its new episodes go in sha256(seed, key) order. Episodes already in the file keep their split.

known_limits: Language: the two instruction templates are AutoFly's, verbatim, including the original's spelling "avioding" ('advance to {target} while avioding {obstacle} and other obstacles'); with one obstacle phrase per scene, every instruction is a function of the scene and the target. No paraphrases.

The state is partly privileged: state[0] (distance) and state[1] (bearing) are computed from the target's true position, which the drone cannot observe: a policy that reads them can fly to the target without the image or the instruction. They are AutoFly's own definition, kept as the record's; zero or drop them for a policy that should navigate from the image and the instruction.

state[1] bearing_to_target_rad, state[4] vertical_velocity_m_s, state[5] yaw_rate_rad_s follow best-fit definitions that could not be verified against AutoFly's released episodes (status not_autofly_verified; dataset/state.py).
Kenney low-poly stand-ins stand for vehicles and people where no photoreal model was available (target_stand_in; 682 episodes here). A later Fab session may replace them.

Only successful, collision-free episodes are kept; failures stay in each store's rejects. The SAC experts are below the paper's 0.95 success on several scenes, so each scene's data covers the starts its expert could fly (kept-rates: s01_c1 0.8772, s01_c2 0.9615, s01_c3 0.9804, s01_c4 0.9615, s01d_c1 0.8929, s01d_c2 0.9091, s01d_c3 0.8197, s01d_c4 0.8929, s02_c1 0.8065, s02_c2 0.8065, s02_c3 0.7576, s02_c4 0.7812, s03_c1 0.641, s03_c2 0.641, s03_c3 0.6494, s03_c4 0.6329, s04_c1 0.5263, s04_c2 0.5495, s04_c3 0.5208, s04_c4 0.5435, s05_c1 0.4854, s05_c2 0.5747, s05_c3 0.463, s05_c4 0.5952, s06_c1 0.3876, s06_c2 0.3472, s06_c3 0.3731, s06_c4 0.3968, s07_c1 1.0, s07_c2 0.9259, s07_c3 1.0, s07_c4 1.0, s09_c1 0.8772, s09_c2 0.9804, s09_c3 0.9615, s09_c4 1.0). The actions are the expert's (stochastic where the pilot record says deterministic false), not a human's.

The val split is a stratified random sample of the same scenes and targets: an in-distribution validation set, not a test of unseen scenes or targets (test_seen and test_unseen are evaluated in closed loop).
Per-step phase weights from the rebalancing stage (spec §10.3) are not part of the records.

loading.tfds: tfds.builder_from_directory('<out>/autofly_ue5_proto/1.0.0'), or tfds.builder('autofly_ue5_proto', data_dir='<out>') as OpenVLA calls it
loading.openvla: image_obs_keys {'primary': 'image_0'}, state_obs_keys ['state'], language_key 'language_instruction'; the action is 3-dim, so pass action_normalization_mask [True]*3 and no absolute_action_mask (OpenVLA's make_oxe_dataset_kwargs assumes 7-dim EEF actions); dataset_statistics.json[name] is the normalisation (BOUNDS_Q99 uses q01 and q99)
